chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn Saeed, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A group of men participated in buying a slave girl, so they entrusted one of them and left the girl with him, and he had intercourse with her. He (peace be upon him) said: He is whipped with the penalty (Hadd), and the penalty is deferred from him by the measure of his share in her. The girl is evaluated, and her price is paid to the partners. If her value on the day he had intercourse with her is less than what she was bought for, he is liable for the excess of the price because he has spoiled her for his partners; and if her value on the day he had intercourse with her is more than what she was bought for, he is liable for the excess due to spoiling her.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for a partner who has intercourse with a jointly owned slave girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudence of 'Iqar' (consanguineous partnership) in slave ownership, where a partner's unilateral sexual act is treated as a breach of trust causing financial depreciation. It establishes that the offender receives the Hadd penalty adjusted for his share and must compensate the co-owners based on the difference between the purchase price and the post-act valuation, ensuring the loss is borne by the transgressor. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on property rights and the economic consequences of unilateral actions within joint ownership structures.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A group participated in buying a slave girl, so they relied upon one of them, and made the slave girl to be with him, so he went to her’. Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) and it would be staved off by the measurement of whatever (share) was for him in her, and the slave girl would be evaluated, and her price would be for the associates. So if her price during the day she had been copulated with is less than what she was bought for, so the excess of the price would be necessitated upon him, because he had spoilt upon his associates; and if it was that the price during the day which she had been copulated with is more than what she had been bought for, the excess would be necessitated for having spoilt her’.
